articles.title: Federal regulator probing Trump critic Adam Kinzinger for betting on his own pardon
articles.summary: Federal regulators are investigating former Rep. Adam Kinzinger for trading on the prediction platform Kalshi about a pardon he received from former Presiden...
articles.body:
Federal regulators are investigating former Rep. Adam Kinzinger for trading on the prediction platform Kalshi about a pardon he received from former President Joe Biden, two sources familiar with the matter told CNN.

Biden pardoned Kinzinger last year during the final hours of his presidency, along with other members of the House committee that investigated Donald Trump's attempts to overturn the 2020 election. The preemptive pardons were needed, Biden argued, to protect the lawmakers from possible retaliation by the incoming Trump administration.

Prediction platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket let users wager on nearly everything – including sports, entertainment, elections and other political news.

Kinzinger, a Republican and prominent Trump critic, traded less than $1,000 on two pardon-related Kalshi markets in late 2024 and early 2025, sources said, and betted that he would get a pardon from Biden.

He acknowledged making the trades in an interview with CNN but said he never had any insider information about the pardons. He was a private citizen at the time of the trades – out of Congress and not running for office. Kinzinger is a CNN contributor.

A person familiar with the matter said the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal regulator that polices prediction markets, is looking into Kinzinger's trades. Career enforcement officials started scrutinizing the Biden pardon markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket after seeing press reports about potential insider activity, the source said.

Politico previously reported the CFTC inquiry into Kinzinger, which is the first publicly known federal probe into pardon markets on prediction sites.

CNN has maintained a partnership with Kalshi since December and uses its data to cover major events, but CNN editorial employees aren't permitted to use prediction markets.

The CFTC and Kalshi declined to comment.

In an interview with CNN, Kinzinger admitted to making the trades, saying they were two of a "few dozen" bets he placed about political topics. He said he had reviewed Kalshi's rules beforehand and that he believed his actions did not violate the rules. He shared screenshots with CNN showing that he wagered a total of $669 and netted $823.

"It was a dumb bet, to bet on myself," Kinzinger said. "Looking back, I'm like, yeah, I wish I'd have skipped it. But everything I saw at the time was like, you're within your right to bet on this."

He also denied that he engaged in insider trading, primarily because he says he did not have any advance knowledge of the pardons and did not discuss potential pardons with the Biden White House. He said he hasn't heard from any government investigators.

"At no point, ever, had I had a conversation with anybody in the know about pardons (or) whether I'd get pardoned," Kinzinger said. "Certainly, nobody in the White House or anybody that would know anything."

Kalshi also uncovered Kinzinger's trades during a broader look into "suspicious" activity and flagged them to the CFTC, another person familiar with the matter said.

The source said Kalshi tried to get in touch with Kinzinger, but he did not respond. It's common for Kalshi to try to internally settle its probes when small amounts of money are involved and when the trader cooperates. Kinzinger told CNN he never heard from Kalshi.

Prediction platforms have exploded in popularity this year and now see billions of dollars in weekly trading volume. But as they've grown, so have calls for more regulation.

Last month, Kalshi fined several political candidates for betting on their own campaigns, violating the company's insider-trading rules.

The CFTC also recently settled a case with the former Trump White House teleprompter operator for "unlawful" bets on Kalshi about what Trump would say in his speeches. And they settled with former Rep. George Santos for improper trades about whether he would attend the State of the Union.

A bipartisan coalition of 44 states have urged the CFTC to rein in prediction platforms. So have dozens of lawmakers on Capitol Hill, who are backing legislation that would stiffen penalties against insider trading.

Among those who want more regulation is Kinzinger himself. He wrote in a November 2025 Substack post that Kalshi and other prediction sites are a "corruption time bomb" and a "threat to democracy" because politicians can profit from insider knowledge.

articles.title: Celulares em presídios: Operação apreende 598 aparelhos em uma semana | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação do Ministério da Justiça mobilizou 4,2 mil policiais penais e fez revistas em 3,6 mil celas de 107 unidades prisionais.
articles.summary: A apreensão de celulares em presídios durante a Operação MUTE mobilizou 4,2 mil policiais para combater a comunicação do crime organizado em todo o país.
articles.body:
Uma operação nacional em presídios apreendeu 598 celulares na última semana, segundo informou o Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública nesta quinta-feira (1º).

A ação foi realizada em mais de 100 estabelecimentos prisionais em todos os estados e no Distrito Federal.

Segundo a pasta, policiais federais e estaduais fizeram revistas orientadas em 3.604 celas, durante operação realizada entre 21 e 25 de setembro. As unidades visitadas abrigam mais de 88 mil pessoas detidas.

A operação tem como objetivo combater a entrada e a circulação de materiais proibidos nos presídios e, principalmente, interromper a comunicação entre criminosos que estão presos e integrantes de organizações criminosas que permanecem em liberdade.

A Operação MUTE, coordenada pela Secretaria Nacional de Políticas Penais (Senappen), utiliza informações de inteligência para identificar e retirar celulares e outros materiais ilícitos dos presídios .

Segundo o ministério, desde maio, operações como essa apreenderam 3.045 celulares dentro de presídios. A ação faz parte de um esforço concentrado contra o crime organizado.

articles.summary: O advogado Rafael Marchiani Paião, de 42 anos, que morreu após a cobertura de uma quadra de tênis desabar durante um temporal em Umuarama (PR), foi sepultado em Rancharia (SP).
articles.body:
Advogado morreu atingido por cobertura de clube de tênis — Foto: Redes sociais

O advogado Rafael Marchiani Paião, de 42 anos, que morreu após a cobertura de uma quadra de tênis desabar durante um temporal em Umuarama (PR), foi sepultado na manhã desta quinta-feira (1º), em sua cidade natal, Rancharia (SP).

O acidente ocorreu na tarde de terça-feira (29), quando Rafael praticava esporte e o telhado cedeu. O velório foi realizado na manhã de quarta-feira (30), em Umuarama, e o sepultamento ocorreu no Cemitério Santo Antônio, em Rancharia.

Segundo o Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar), as rajadas de vento no momento da queda atingiram 67 km/h, chegando a 101,5 km/h ao longo do dia do acidente.

O advogado era especialista em Direito Eleitoral e Público e atuava como coordenador jurídico em uma campanha eleitoral. Além disso, era sócio do clube onde ocorreu o desabamento.

Pelas redes sociais, o Harmonia Clube de Campo lamentou a morte do advogado e prestou solidariedade aos familiares da vítima.

A Polícia Civil de Umuarama informou que instaurou inquérito e investiga o caso.

articles.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro apresenta nova revisão ao STF e pede suspensão da pena | G1
articles.standfirst: Advogados citam parecer que aponta problemas na verificação de provas digitais e manifestações recentes de ministros do STF; revisão foi apresentada em 25 de setembro e pede anulação da condenação.
articles.summary: Advogados citam parecer que aponta problemas na verificação de provas digitais e manifestações recentes de ministros do STF; revisão foi apresentada em 25 de setembro e pede anulação da condenação.
articles.body:
A defesa do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL) apresentou uma nova revisão criminal ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para tentar anular a condenação de 27 anos e três meses pela trama golpista e voltou a pedir a suspensão da execução da pena .

🔎 A revisão criminal é uma ação que permite contestar uma condenação que já se tornou definitiva, em situações previstas em lei, como diante do surgimento de novas provas.

A nova ação, apresentada em 25 de setembro, cita como “prova nova” um parecer técnico que, segundo os advogados, identificou problemas na cadeia de custódia e limitações para verificar parte das provas digitais utilizadas no processo.

"Não se objetiva, esclareça-se desde logo, um segundo julgamento do feito; a presente Revisão está sendo proposta em razão de fatos novos, prova nova e a demonstração cabal de que a manutenção da condenação de Jair Bolsonaro representa grave injustiça", afirmou a defesa.

🔎 A cadeia de custódia é o conjunto de procedimentos usados para registrar e acompanhar uma prova desde sua obtenção até sua utilização no processo. No caso de provas digitais, esse controle permite verificar, por exemplo, a origem e a integridade dos arquivos.

A defesa também usa manifestações recentes de ministros do STF sobre investigações e análise de grandes volumes de dados para sustentar os pedidos de nulidade.

O parecer não afirma que houve adulteração das provas. O argumento da defesa é que, em parte do material analisado, não foi possível verificar integralmente a origem e o processamento dos dados.

"Ao tempo do processo, a defesa fixou teses importantes quando do recebimento da denúncia e nas alegações finais. Repetiu, de forma até insistente, que o processo penal ora sob revisão havia violado o princípio acusatório; a defesa deixou claro que não houve tempo de analisar a prova, entregue horas antes da instrução, que perdurou por cerca de uma quinzena; e que a cadeia de custódia, naquelas condições, jamais poderia ser verificada", argumentou a defesa.

"Verificou-se agora. E um parecer técnico deixa assentado que há comprometimento da cadeia de custódia, que, como é verdadeiramente óbvio, não poderia ser conferida no tempo que foi dado à defesa", prosseguiu.

A peça pede distribuição por prevenção ao ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, relator de outra revisão criminal apresentada pela defesa de Bolsonaro em maio deste ano contra a mesma condenação.

Na prática, a distribuição por prevenção faz com que um processo relacionado a outro já em andamento seja encaminhado ao mesmo relator. A defesa argumentou que as duas revisões tratam da mesma condenação e de questões relacionadas.

Os advogados mantiveram aquela revisão em tramitação. Na nova ação, apresentada na sexta (25), voltaram a pedir a suspensão da pena.

Entenda a cronologia da estratégia da defesa

24/9: pediu suspensão → desistiu da suspensão → manteve a revisão.

25/9: apresentou nova revisão → voltou a pedir suspensão da pena.

O ex-presidente da República, Jair Messias Bolsonaro (PL), fez uma aparição de cerca de 20 minutos no quintal da casa onde ele cumpria prisão domiciliar em 9 de setembro de 2025 — Foto: Wilton Junior/Estadão Conteúdo

articles.title: Master: PF deve pedir posição de Fachin sobre citações a ministros | G1
articles.standfirst: Fontes ligadas à PF ouvidas pelo blog afirmam que o caso está no limite da exposição. Entre os ministros que apareceram, em diferentes contextos, no material ou nas discussões em torno do caso Master, estão: Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, Luiz Fux e Kassio Nunes Marques.
articles.summary: A Polícia Federal apresentará ao ministro Edson Fachin um relatório sobre as menções a integrantes da Corte nas investigações envolvendo o Banco Master e Daniel Vorcaro.
articles.body:
Presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin em sessão plenária extraordinária do STF - 15/09/2026 — Foto: Rosinei Coutinho/STF

Fontes da Polícia Federal ouvidas pelo blog afirmam que a corporação deve levar ao ministro Edson Fachin , presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), um relatório com a posição da corporação a respeito das citações a ministros do Supremo que vieram a público nas investigações envolvendo Daniel Vorcaro e o Banco Master, para que o presidente da Corte decida o que fazer.

A avaliação dentro da PF, segundo essas fontes, é que o caso está no limite público da exposição -- e que, para dar qualquer continuidade ao que está colocado, é preciso de uma resposta do presidente da corte, Edson Fachin.

Vieram a público menções a ministros e informações sobre relações deles com Vorcaro ou pessoas ligadas ao grupo Master. Ao mesmo tempo, aumentou a pressão para que a polícia dê algum encaminhamento a esse material.

Diante desse cenário, investigadores dizem que o entendimento é levar a situação ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, para que ele decida o que deve ser feito em relação aos ministros citados.

A ideia é repetir, agora de forma ainda mais amarrada institucionalmente, o caminho adotado no caso de Dias Toffoli no início do ano: ministros acusaram a PF de decidir por conta própria avançar sobre o integrante do STF. E, para investigar um ministro do STF, o material precisa ser submetido à cúpula da Corte para uma definição sobre os próximos passos. A PF nega que tenha feito isso.

Entre os ministros que apareceram, em diferentes contextos, no material ou nas discussões em torno do caso Master, estão: Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, Luiz Fux e Kassio Nunes Marques. As citações, por si só, não significam participação em irregularidades.

Esse ponto é importante porque, desde o início da crise, existe uma disputa sobre quem pode investigar ministros do Supremo e em quais circunstâncias. A própria PF foi alvo de críticas no episódio envolvendo Toffoli, inclusive depois do vazamento de uma reunião sobre o caso.

O que se espera agora é a confirmação de uma agenda com o presidente do STF. A PF pretende levar a Fachin o material, expor sua posição e pedir que seja ele a definir qual deve ser o encaminhamento em relação aos ministros mencionados.

A avaliação resumida por uma fonte é: “Chegou no limite.”

Com o que já veio a público e a pressão por uma resposta, a PF entende que não pode simplesmente ignorar o material — mas a ideia é colocar o caso nas mãos de Fachin para que ele decida o que fazer.

articles.title: Caso Nossa Senhora: André Mendonça muda voto no TSE após acordo | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministros alertaram André Mendonça que versão inicial do voto poderia atingir liberdade de expressão; Acordo também deixou solução do caso no próprio TSE enfraquecendo eventual atuação posterior do STF
articles.summary: André Mendonça alterou seu voto no TSE para garantir a liberdade de expressão e evitar a interferência do STF no caso das postagens de Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.body:
A decisão do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) sobre o caso Nossa Senhora aconteceu depois de muitas conversas entre ministros e de um acordo que deu sinais em várias direções.

O ministro André Mendonça , relator do caso, conversou com o presidente do TSE, ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, e com vários ministros da Corte, e foi só a partir daí que ele decidiu mudar o voto.

Primeiro, o ministro tinha votado a favor da retirada de mais de mil postagens que ele entendia que associavam o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) à informação inverídica envolvendo nossa Senhora Aparecida, inclusive o post do humorista Antonio Tabet. Ele é o relator do caso.

Na postagem, o humorista escreveu, sem citar Flávio Bolsonaro, que "a família miliciana odeia tanto mulher preta, que resolveu atacar Nossa Senhora Aparecida".

Depois, ele liberou o post de Tabet, reformulando seu voto e deixando mais claro o argumento da liberdade de expressão.

Ao rever seu entendimento, Mendonça modificou o voto para liberar a postagem sob argumento de que o texto não atribui a Flávio uma ação concreta contra a imagem ou o título de Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

"Diante da razoabilidade da compreensão de ambiguidade de seu conteúdo, entendo que a solução mais consentânea com os critérios de intervenção mínima e de proteção reforçada da liberdade de expressão consiste em preservar a postagem", diz Mendonça.

O ministro do STF e futuro vice-presidente do TSE, André Mendonça — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/Secom/TSE

Isso só aconteceu depois de muitas conversas internas. Ministros alertaram o relator que não mudar de voto implicaria passar mensagem duvidosa sobre liberdade de expressão, e tirar um post de um humorista que não cita o candidato deixaria isso muito claro.

Além disso, estava claro internamente que, se ele mudasse, seria uma solução doméstica pra crise, enfraquecendo a atuação do STF posteriormente.

Essa atuação do STF foi feita até agora por dois ministros: Flavio Dino, que derrubou a primeira decisão monocrática de Mendonça; e Luiz Fux, que retomou a decisão de Mendonça.

Os dois pediram pro caso ir ao plenário, o que sinalizava que era o STF a dar a palavra final. O presidente do TSE, Nunes Marques, reclamou ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, que havia uma sobreposição do Supremo sobre a atuação da Justiça Eleitoral.

Como o blog revelou, ao receber essa reclamação, Fachin pediu a Nunes que resolvesse essa questão primeiro no TSE para minimizar as chances de essa nova crise depender de desfecho do STF – que já tem a crise do Master para lidar.

Foi assim que Nunes Marques decidiu marcar a decisão para o plenário virtual do TSE. E após esse acordo institucional, depois houve um novo acordo sobre o voto do ministro Mendonça, que topou mudar.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: 25 escolas municipais serão seções eleitorais em PP | G1
articles.standfirst: Devido aos preparativos para as eleições, os alunos serão dispensados mais cedo nesta sexta-feira (2). Eleitores aptos podem consultar o lugar de votação pelo site do TRE ou pelo aplicativo.
articles.summary: Nas eleições de 2026, cuja votação ocorre neste domingo (4), 25 escolas municipais serão utilizadas como locais de votação em Presidente Prudente (SP).
articles.body:
25 escolas municipais serão seções eleitorais em Prudente — Foto: g1

Nas eleições de 2026, cuja votação ocorre neste domingo (4), 25 escolas municipais serão utilizadas como locais de votação em Presidente Prudente (SP).

Segundo a prefeitura, devido aos preparativos para o primeiro turno, os alunos serão dispensados às 15h desta sexta-feira (2). O horário será antecipado para que as salas que serão usadas pelos eleitores sejam organizadas.

Caso haja segundo turno, a votação será realizada no domingo, 25 de outubro. Nesse caso, os alunos da rede municipal também serão dispensados às 15h da sexta-feira (23) que antecede a eleição.

Das 25 escolas municipais que serão utilizadas, 15 pertencem à 101ª Zona Eleitoral e dez à 402ª Zona Eleitoral, conforme as diretrizes do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

Há também escolas particulares e universidades do município que serão utilizadas como locais de votação.

A Prefeitura de Presidente Prudente também oferece transporte público gratuito aos fins de semana, que poderá ser utilizado pelos eleitores para chegar aos locais de votação.

Conforme o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), é possível consultar o local de votação no site oficial do TSE ou pelo aplicativo e-Título, digitando o número do CPF.

Escolher no menu "Consultas" a opção "Onde votar";

Acrescentar o CPF, data de nascimento e o nome da mãe.

Já a consulta do número do título eleitoral é possível no site oficial do TSE. As etapas são:

Na parte de “Autenticação”, é necessário informar o CPF, data de nascimento e nome do pai ou da mãe.

Confira abaixo as seções em prédios municipais:

Os candidatos que concorrem nas eleições de 4 de outubro, no 1º turno, não podem ser detidos ou presos até 6 de outubro. A prisão nesse período só pode acontecer em caso de flagrante delito.

A proteção está prevista no Código Eleitoral: os candidatos não podem ser presos a partir de 15 dias antes da eleição até 48 horas depois da votação.

A medida também vale para o segundo turno, marcado para 25 de outubro: nenhum candidato que ainda estiver concorrendo poderá ser detido ou preso entre 10 e 27 de outubro, a não ser em caso de flagrante delito.

Conforme destacam vários tribunais regionais eleitorais, o objetivo é assegurar o equilíbrio da disputa, evitando que eventuais prisões sejam realizadas com o objetivo de prejudicar candidatos.

O flagrante delito acontece quando alguém é surpreendido cometendo um crime ou logo após tê-lo praticado. Boca de urna e compra de votos, por exemplo, são crimes eleitorais que permitem a prisão em flagrante.

Se ocorrer a prisão de um candidato, ele deverá ser imediatamente conduzido à presença de um juiz competente, que irá avaliar a legalidade da detenção. Se constatar ilegalidade, o juiz deverá determinar a soltura imediata, além de poder responsabilizar o autor da prisão.

Mesmo que a detenção em flagrante delito seja confirmada, o candidato poderá concorrer às eleições, pois a legislação exige condenação por órgão colegiado ou trânsito em julgado (condenação definitiva) para impedir o direito de disputa.

A "imunidade" também vale para os eleitores, mas por um período menor: de acordo com o Código Eleitoral, nenhum eleitor poderá ser preso a partir de cinco dias antes das eleições até 48 horas depois da votação.

Assim, os eleitores não podem ser detidos ou presos entre 29 de setembro e 6 de outubro — pois o primeiro turno acontece em 4 de outubro.

Também não podem ser detidos ou presos entre 20 e 27 de outubro, já que o segundo turno ocorre no dia 25 desse mês.

O objetivo é evitar que o cidadão seja impedido de exercer seu direito ao voto. A origem dessa proteção remonta ao primeiro Código Eleitoral do país, de 1932, que buscava evitar a intimidação dos eleitores pelos “coronéis” (chefes políticos regionais da época).

Mas há três casos em que o eleitor poderá ser detido ou preso nesse período:

sentença criminal condenatória por crime inafiançável (decisão definitiva da Justiça que condena alguém por um crime grave, para o qual a lei não permite o pagamento de fiança);

desrespeito a salvo-conduto (quando alguém descumpre uma ordem da Justiça Eleitoral que protege outro eleitor contra ameaças ou coerção para votar, para não votar ou por já ter votado).

Mesários e fiscais de partido têm direito à imunidade eleitoral, mas somente enquanto estiverem exercendo suas funções (nos dias das votações).

Apesar dessa proteção, eles poderão ser detidos ou presos em caso de flagrante delito.

articles.title: Eleições 2026 na Paraíba: aulas em escolas e universidades mudam | G1
articles.standfirst: Algumas delas serão cedidas à Justiça Eleitoral para a votação.
articles.summary: As Eleições 2026 na Paraíba alteram o funcionamento de instituições como UFPB, UEPB e redes municipais, que cedem prédios para votação e retomam aulas na segunda-feira.
articles.body:
Eleições 2026: veja como ficam as aulas em escolas e universidades da PB antes e depois do 1º turno — Foto: Prefeitura de Patos/Divulgação

Parte das escolas e universidades da Paraíba terá mudanças no funcionamento por causa do primeiro turno das Eleições 2026 , que acontece no próximo domingo (4). As alterações ocorrem porque algumas unidades que são locais de votação serão cedidas à Justiça Eleitoral.

O g1 te explica quais são as mudanças no horário de funcionamento das principais instituições públicas de ensino das redes federal, estadual e municipal (no caso dos três maiores colégios eleitorais da Paraíba: João Pessoa , Campina Grande e Santa Rita ). Veja abaixo as alterações adotadas .

Universidade Federal da Paraíba (UFPB), campus João Pessoa — Foto: Krystine Carneiro/G1

A Universidade Federal da Paraíba (UFPB) vai manter o expediente normal na sexta-feira (2) e na segunda-feira (5). Algumas salas da Central de Aulas, do CCHLA e do CCSA serão cedidas para a realização do pleito, mas a medida não vai afetar o funcionamento das atividades da instituição.

Centro de Ciências Jurídicas (CCJ) da UEPB — Foto: Divulgação/UEPB

A Universidade Estadual da Paraíba (UEPB) terá as atividades liberadas a partir das 13h da sexta-feira (2) e o funcionamento será retomado às 13h da segunda-feira (5), conforme portaria da instituição.

A medida vale para os campi e unidades que serão utilizados pela Justiça Eleitoral durante o primeiro turno.

De acordo com informações do TRE-PB, há locais de votação em prédios específicos da UEPB; são eles:

Campina Grande: Centro de Ciências Jurídicas (CCJ), no Centro da cidade, próximo ao Açude Velho;

Araruna : prédio antigo e prédio novo do Campus VIII.

Universidade Federal de Campina Grande (UFCG)

Universidade oferece 35 vagas em seleção para professor substituto. — Foto: UFCG

A Universidade Federal de Campina Grande (UFCG) terá algumas dependências do Campus Sede disponibilizadas à Justiça Eleitoral a partir das 7h da sexta-feira (2) até o domingo (4).

Os espaços utilizados serão a Unidade Acadêmica de Línguas, os blocos BC, BD, BG e BZ e a Unidade Acadêmica de Música (UNAMUS).

Durante esse período, os blocos ficarão isolados e não poderão ser utilizados para atividades acadêmicas.

Além disso, não deverão ser realizadas atividades nas unidades da instituição nos dias 3 e 4 de outubro, exceto aquelas consideradas estritamente necessárias.

A universidade informou que, na segunda-feira (5), as atividades serão retomadas normalmente.

Os campi do Instituto Federal da Paraíba (IFPB) que serão utilizados pela Justiça Eleitoral serão cedidos a partir da sexta-feira (2). — Foto: Divulgação/IFPB

Os campi do Instituto Federal da Paraíba (IFPB) que serão utilizados pela Justiça Eleitoral serão cedidos a partir da sexta-feira (2).

As atividades serão retomadas normalmente na segunda-feira (5).

Escola Estadual Cidadã Técnica de Campina Grande Professor Braulio Maia Júnior — Foto: Reprodução/TV Paraíba

As escolas da rede estadual que serão utilizadas como locais de votação serão entregues à Justiça Eleitoral na quinta-feira (1º).

As aulas serão retomadas normalmente na segunda-feira (5).

Escolas da rede municipal de João Pessoa

Escola municipal em João Pessoa — Foto: Dayse Euzébio/Secom-JP/Divulgação

A rede municipal de João Pessoa irá ceder 81 escolas e seis Ninhos do Saber à Justiça Eleitoral a partir da quinta-feira (1º), para a organização dos locais de votação e instalação das urnas eletrônicas.

As unidades serão devolvidas à Secretaria de Educação e Cultura (Sedec) na segunda-feira (5), e as aulas devem ser retomadas no turno da tarde, após a limpeza e reorganização dos espaços.

Nas unidades que não serão cedidas à Justiça Eleitoral, as aulas acontecem normalmente até sexta-feira (2) e também na segunda-feira (5).

Escolas da rede municipal de Campina Grande

Escola Municipal Félix Araújo, em Campina Grande — Foto: Lídice Pegado/TV Paraíba

A rede municipal de Campina Grande irá disponibilizar 67 escolas à Justiça Eleitoral a partir da quinta-feira (1º) até o sábado (3), de forma graduada. As aulas devem ser retomadas normalmente na segunda-feira (5).

A rede municipal de ensino de Santa Rita disponibilizou, no dia 25 de setembro, prédios de algumas escolas à Justiça Eleitoral para a preparação e realização das eleições de 2026. Com isso, as aulas nessas unidades ficam suspensas até segunda-feira (5).

De acordo com a Secretaria Municipal de Educação, as atividades escolares serão retomadas normalmente na terça-feira (6).

articles.title: White House removes CNN from press pool for Trump’s upcoming trip to Texas and Oklahoma
articles.summary: CNN was previously scheduled to fly on Air Force One and also provide on-the-ground coverage of Trump’s trip.
articles.body:
The White House on Wednesday removed CNN from the press pool that's set to cover a trip by President Donald Trump on Thursday, escalating a feud with the cable network after a federal judge blocked the administration's push to restrict its media access.

CNN had been designated to travel with Trump on Thursday, according to a press rotation document the White House released Sunday. But when the daily guidance came out for his scheduled visit to a truck manufacturing facility in Denton, Texas, followed by remarks in Durant, Oklahoma, it did not list CNN as providing pool coverage.

The move comes less than a week after a federal judge halted Trump's effort to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. It also comes after the White House barred CNN from flying on Air Force One over the weekend when Trump traveled to Tennessee, when the network was scheduled to provide pool coverage. (The judge's order was limited to media access on the White House grounds.)

Emily Kuhn, a spokesperson for CNN, confirmed the cable network's removal from planned pool coverage but did not provide additional comment. Instead, she pointed to an earlier statement from Theodore Boutrous, an attorney representing CNN, MS NOW and Politico in their fight with the White House over press access, calling the ban "a blatant violation of the First Amendment and due process."

In a statement Thursday, Boutrous said that "the White House is persisting in unpredictably and inconsistently implementing the President's unconstitutional 'ban on the free press' by barring CNN from fulfilling its role as a designated television network pooler—to the detriment of CNN, its fellow pool members and, ultimately, the American public."

The three news outlets he represents on Monday asked a federal judge to extend his pause on Trump's ban.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about CNN's exclusion from Thursday's trip.

The White House press pool is a group of media outlets that share video, editorial information and costs for coverage of high-profile officials and events involving the president anywhere in the world. Under the system, each day's designated "poolers" represent the wider press corps to document newsworthy events and serve as a conduit between the president and the public.

The White House Correspondents' Association, the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press and a group of 49 news and media organizations that included NBCUniversal Media, the parent company of NBC News, filed a legal brief last week in support of CNN, MS NOW and Politico.

Other member networks of the pool — Fox News, ABC News, CBS News and NBC News — briefly boycotted participating in pool duties last week in solidarity with CNN.

NBC News did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the exclusion of CNN for Thursday's trip and whether it intended to take any action.

Trump has restricted access for other news outlets before. In 2025, he banned The Associated Press from the Oval Office, Air Force One and certain events for not referring to the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America — his preferred name for the gulf.

articles.standfirst: El seleccionador de la República Checa atendió a 'La Tribu' antes de medirse a España y aseguró que el equipo de De la Fuente es “la mejor selección y el mejor equipo” del mundo
articles.summary: El seleccionador de la República Checa atendió a 'La Tribu' antes de medirse a España y aseguró que el equipo de De la Fuente es “la mejor selección y el mejor equipo” del mundo
articles.body: Santi Denia atendió a La Tribu antes de enfrentarse a España en el Tartiere. El actual seleccionador de la República Checa, pieza clave durante años en la estructura de la Federación Española, explicó cómo está construyendo su nuevo proyecto y reconoció la dificultad de medirse a un equipo que conoce muy bien por dentro y que considera la gran referencia del fútbol mundial. El técnico español aterrizó en Chequia con una idea clara: aplicar parte de la experiencia acumulada durante 15 años en la Federación Española. “Les explicamos nuestra idea, nuestra experiencia en la Federación y el desarrollo que veíamos”, señaló Denia, que trabaja para cambiar estructuras, protocolos y reforzar el sentido de pertenencia dentro de una selección con historia y margen de crecimiento. Denia insistió en que su objetivo no pasa solo por competir de inmediato, sino por crear una selección reconocible. “Queremos que intente jugar al fútbol, que compita bien y que gane partidos”, explicó. Para el técnico, la victoria es el objetivo final, pero siempre dentro de “un modelo de juego reconocible”, una idea clara y un perfil de jugador determinado. El seleccionador también explicó que su cuerpo técnico está todavía en una fase de conocimiento profundo del país, de sus futbolistas y de su esencia. “Ese es un poco el trabajo del seleccionador: elegir a los mejores, no es tanto el entrenamiento, sino seleccionar bien”, apuntó. Preguntado por el nivel de España, Denia fue tajante. “No hay duda, es el mejor equipo del mundo”, aseguró. Y quiso hacer una doble distinción: España es, para él, “la mejor selección y el mejor equipo”, por la calidad de sus jugadores y por la capacidad de Luis de la Fuente para convertir esas individualidades en un bloque. Ahí situó una de las grandes claves del éxito español: “Lo que mejor tienes que hacer es seleccionar. Y cuando seleccionas, lo que tienes que lograr es hacer un equipo”. Denia destacó que Luis de la Fuente ha conseguido que “todos tiren para el mismo lado” y que cada jugador salga “con la misma convicción” y “el mismo compromiso”. El técnico incluso aceptó la comparación con la España de 2010: “Está para compararla con la selección de 2010 o incluso mejor”. Para Denia, esta España gana porque es “el mejor equipo”, no solo porque tenga grandes jugadores. Denia también habló de Lamine Yamal, uno de los grandes nombres propios de esta España. Preguntado por si el futbolista del Barcelona es ahora mismo el mejor del mundo y si debe llevarse el Balón de Oro, el seleccionador de la República Checa no dejó lugar a dudas: “Sí, sin ninguna duda”. “Da igual que tenga 19 años”, añadió Denia, que defendió que el presente debe pesar más que la edad a la hora de valorar al jugador. “En el momento, en el presente, es el mejor”, aseguró. Para el técnico, no hay que mirar el DNI cuando un futbolista ya está preparado para competir al máximo nivel: “Si juegas en el Barcelona con 17 años, es porque estás preparado”. El gran momento llegó al hablar del duelo directo con Luis de la Fuente. Denia conoce perfectamente al seleccionador español y sabe que el partido tendrá mucho de pizarra, lectura y ajustes. “Va a ser una partida de ajedrez con Luis. Tú mueves este, yo voy a mover este”, explicó. El seleccionador checo dejó claro que su equipo no saldrá únicamente a resistir. “Hay que gestionar todo: presión alta, bloque medio, bloque bajo, defensa de área, transición... Si solo te metes en bloque bajo, te van a ganar”, advirtió. Su plan pasa por analizar a España, fortalecer lo que Chequia hace bien y minimizar sus debilidades. Santi Denia espera reencontrarse con Luis de la Fuente en Oviedo, donde ambos se darán “un buen abrazo”. Después llegará el fútbol. Una partida de ajedrez entre dos técnicos que se conocen, con España como gigante mundial y Chequia intentando crecer sin renunciar a competir.

articles.title: Will Democrats move beyond rhetoric on Israel’s illegal settlements?
articles.summary: A new E1 sanctions bill could test whether US objections are finally backed by consequences.
articles.body:
A shift is taking place in Washington. Senate Democrats are moving to sanction individuals and entities involved in Israel’s E1 settlement project, one of the most consequential efforts to reshape the occupied West Bank. The timing is significant. Reports that the project may have been put on hold raise the question of whether the pause represents a substantive policy change or merely a tactical delay. Meanwhile, the Senate is preparing to leave Washington this week, narrowing the immediate window for action. The question is no longer simply whether Democrats object to illegal settlement expansion, but whether they are prepared to turn those objections into consequences.

The legislation, introduced on September 23 by Senators Chris Coons, Elizabeth Warren, Ron Wyden and Ruben Gallego, would target individuals and entities involved in facilitating settlement construction in E1. It has at least 10 Democratic cosponsors and was referred to the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee.

E1 lies between occupied East Jerusalem and the major illegal settlement of Maale Adumim. Its development has long been viewed by Palestinian officials, foreign governments and advocates of a two-state solution as particularly consequential because construction there could disrupt territorial continuity between northern and southern parts of the occupied West Bank while further isolating East Jerusalem. The issue, therefore, is not simply another settlement project, but whether the geography of the West Bank is being altered in ways that could make Palestinian territorial self-determination increasingly difficult.

The proposed legislation would impose sanctions on foreign individuals and entities determined by the Treasury Department to have facilitated settlement construction or related activity in E1, including participation in tenders. It would also target those involved in organising, financing or facilitating the transfer of Israeli civilians into illegal settlements in the area.

That would represent a departure from the traditional Washington response. A government can dismiss a diplomatic protest; sanctions affecting companies, individuals or access to the US financial system are harder to ignore. Yet the measure remains a proposal, its prospects are uncertain, and the House of Representatives is out of session. The Senate’s impending departure means the immediate political opportunity is narrowing, although the legislation will remain alive during the recess.

Its significance, therefore, may depend as much on what happens when Congress returns as on what happens before it leaves.

Reports that the E1 project may have been put on hold deserve attention, but also caution. A suspension, delay in tenders or postponement would not necessarily amount to abandonment. Nor would it reverse settlement expansion already approved or resolve the broader question of the West Bank’s territorial future.

If E1 has merely been deferred, Washington should not mistake a pause for a policy change. But if the project has genuinely been halted, the moment presents an opportunity to test whether US pressure can help turn temporary restraint into a durable decision.

That is where sanctions could matter. Their significance would not necessarily lie in punishing a project after the fact, but in establishing that settlement expansion can carry consequences before the process becomes irreversible.

The Democratic debate must also confront the Biden administration’s record. The administration repeatedly stated that settlements were inconsistent with international law and harmful to the prospects for a two-state solution. Yet those objections coexisted with continued military assistance and a broader strategic relationship with Israel. Washington thus continued to articulate support for Palestinian statehood while doing relatively little to prevent developments that could make such a state increasingly difficult to realise.

That contradiction has not been confined to one administration. Successive US governments have often treated settlement expansion as an obstacle to peace while stopping short of using significant leverage to prevent it.

The political environment within the Democratic Party, however, is changing. A growing number of Democratic lawmakers are challenging aspects of Israeli policy, including settlement expansion and pogroms. The E1 legislation reflects a broader debate over whether support for Israel must also mean insulating Israeli government policies from meaningful US consequences.

For the E1 initiative to become more than symbolism, Congress would have to establish clear criteria for sanctions, consistent enforcement and the political willingness to sustain them. More fundamentally, Washington would have to confront the larger framework of its relationship with Israel.

If Palestinian self-determination remains a US policy objective, a basic question follows: what happens when an ally pursues policies that American officials themselves say undermine that objective?

For decades, the answer has mostly been diplomatic objection without corresponding leverage. The proposed sanctions would introduce something largely missing from US settlement policy: the possibility that settlement activity could carry a tangible cost in the United States.

That does not guarantee passage, nor would sanctions by themselves resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. But they would alter the terms of the debate by linking Washington’s stated policy to an instrument capable of imposing consequences.

The E1 initiative should therefore be neither exaggerated nor dismissed. It remains at the beginning of the congressional process, with the House out of session and the Senate preparing to leave Washington. The immediate prospects for enactment may be uncertain. But the more important test is whether its sponsors continue to press the issue after the current political moment has passed.

If E1 has been temporarily put on hold, Washington has an opportunity to press for a permanent halt rather than treating the pause as sufficient. “If the project proceeds, Congress will face a clearer choice over whether settlement activity should continue to be met with statements of concern or tangible consequences.

Ultimately, E1 is about more than a strip of land between Jerusalem and Maale Adumim. It is a test of whether US foreign policy means what it says. Washington has spent decades declaring that settlement expansion undermines Palestinian self-determination and the prospects for a negotiated peace, while rarely attaching a meaningful cost to it.

The E1 legislation offers Democrats an opportunity to begin closing that gap. The decisive question is not whether Washington can issue another warning, but whether it is finally prepared to make its own stated principles matter and make clear that a US commitment to Palestinian self-determination cannot remain a diplomatic phrase while the realities on the ground move in the opposite direction.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: Progressive lawmaker's baby bump photo sparks online firestorm as she faces prison time: 'Disgusting'
articles.summary: Rep. LaMonica McIver's pregnancy announcement while facing 17 years in prison for allegedly assaulting law enforcement sparked fierce backlash online.
articles.body: Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., caused an uproar on social media when she made a post defending her decision to get pregnant despite potentially facing nearly two decades in prison for allegedly assaulting law enforcement officers at Delaney Hall detention center protests. "People might find it crazy that even though I’m facing 17 years in prison, I made the decision to get pregnant," McIver posted to X on Tuesday. "But, at the end of the day, this is something I couldn’t let be consumed by this administration. I refuse to let them take my joy or my future." The New Jersey congresswoman is being charged on three counts of allegedly assaulting, impeding and interfering with law enforcement. The charges stem from McIver's May 2025 visit to Delaney Hall with other Democratic lawmakers. Prosecutors allege McIver physically interfered with federal officers as they attempted to arrest Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. McIver has denied wrongdoing and argued that she was performing congressional oversight. EXCLUSIVE: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN SLAMS SANCTUARY POLITICIANS AS ATTACKS ON ICE OFFICERS SKYROCKET McIver's post prompted several conservative figures and social media users to accuse her of highlighting — or even timing — her pregnancy in hopes of receiving favorable treatment in her criminal case. "When getting pregnant is a social media stunt to avoid prison time...," Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., posted to X. "You violently assaulted a law enforcement officer on camera, then somehow convinced a man to knock you up for political reasons so you could paint yourself as a victim," New Jersey Trump delegate Mike Crispi wrote. "Disgraceful. The poor child." "Why is your pregnancy amid the criminal charges a social media stunt accompanied with a photoshoot?" conservative journalist Andy Ngo said. "Is anyone in your office normal? "Getting pregnant to sway justice is a whole new level of sick," one X user posted. "Why would I find it crazy?" another user said. "You are a cheater & a fraud and, true to character, you became pregnant in an attempt to sway the outcome of the court in your favor." TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT "Facing 17 years, gets pregnant in hope of leniency," another user wrote. "‘I refuse to let them take my joy or my future.’ as the excuse. Congratulations on giving your child the best possible start to life. You are just a genuinely disgusting person." The post comes about a month after a divided federal appeals court allowed two charges against McIver to proceed while sending a third back to the district court for further consideration of her legislative-immunity argument. McIver argued that she should have immunity from prosecution because she was carrying out her duties as a congresswoman in her actions that led to her being charged, calling the charges "vindictive." "Oh stop with the desperate need for sympathy," one posted to X. "YOU are not above the law." "You are on camera assaulting law enforcement," another said. "You are not above the law, you swore to defend it and broke it." One user left a screenshot of a past tweet from McIver where she posted saying, "No one is above the law! Full stop." AOC DOCUMENTS EGG-FREEZING JOURNEY, TAKES AIM AT TRUMP ADMIN OVER WOMEN'S REPRODUCTIVE CHOICES McIver faces multiple felony charges and, if convicted, could face prison time. articles.title: Trump’s red-state tour raises eyebrows and anxiety among Republicans
articles.summary: President Trump’s upcoming campaign stops in a number of red states are raising eyebrows as Democrats seek to expand the midterm map ahead of November’s elections. This week, Trump is slated to visit Oklahoma and Alabama, in addition to making stops in Ohio and Texas. The president is also set to head to Nebraska on…
articles.body:
President Trump’s upcoming campaign stops in a number of red states are raising eyebrows as Democrats seek to expand the midterm map ahead of November’s elections.

This week, Trump is slated to visit Oklahoma and Alabama, in addition to making stops in Ohio and Texas. The president is also set to head to Nebraska on Monday.

Republicans argue the stops are all a part of the party’s strategy to get as close as they can to replicating their 2024 presidential-year turnout.

But polls show voters across the board souring on Trump’s policies, threatening Republican chances in what were once thought to be safe red states like Nebraska.

“I think there are red flashing lights everywhere,” said an unnamed Republican strategist.

Asked in the Oval Office on Wednesday whether the red state tour signals trouble for the GOP heading into the midterms, Trump did not answer directly.

“We have the best economy anywhere in the world,” he said. “There’s no economy like this economy. The only thing we don’t have is good public relations. We don’t seem to be able to get the word across.”

Texas and Ohio are both considered toss-up states in this cycle, but the move for Trump to hold rallies in red strongholds like Alabama and Oklahoma has raised questions about how steep of a climb Republicans up and down the ballot are facing in November.

“Campaigns and presidents don’t spend time where they’re not needed, so that is a data point,” said Scott Tranter, co-founder and director of data science at Decision Desk HQ.

One Republican source cautioned against reading into the visits, noting that the visits are part of a larger strategy of replicating the party’s presidential election turnout as much as they can going into the midterms. The source also described the trip as “hitting two birds with one stone,” noting that Trump’s stops in Oklahoma and Alabama will also play in the Texas and Florida media markets, respectively.

“Nobody can motivate the base like Trump,” said Dan Eberhart, a Republican donor. “I would rather see him in the more competitive Senate race spots like North Carolina, Texas, or Iowa.”

Trump has already visited a number of competitive states already, including Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Georgia. Additionally, Trump has pledged to make campaign stops in 35 competitive races in 30 days.

“It’s obviously a little peculiar,” said one Republican operative, referring to the stops in Alabama and Oklahoma.

But the operative added, “It’s the first of many stops as we know.”

Trump will travel to Mobile, Ala., on Friday, which is divided between the state’s 1st and 2nd congressional districts. House Republicans are targeting Alabama’s 2nd Congressional District, which is represented by Rep. Shomari Figures (D-Ala.), after it was redistricted to benefit Republicans. The GOP nominee, state Rep. Rhett Marques, is slated to speak at the rally even though it is technically in the 1st Congressional District.

The president’s trip to Oklahoma, where he is set to be joined at a rally by his endorsed gubernatorial pick, Mike Mazzei, is also raising eyebrows.

On the surface, Mazzei’s race against Democratic nominee Cyndi Munson appears to be firmly in the GOP column, with the nonpartisan Cook Political Report rating the race as “solid Republican.”

Public polling in the governor’s campaign has been scarce, but Republicans and Democrats note the race may be closer than it appears.

“Democrats have seen polling showing the governor’s race is tied,” said one Democratic operative.

Mazzei campaign spokesperson Jahan Wilcox cited Trump’s endorsement record in a statement to The Hill.

“President Trump has a history of backing winners, and we’re winning. We’re excited to welcome him back to Oklahoma and carry the momentum from his visit through November as Mike Mazzei fights to eliminate the state income tax, abolish property taxes for seniors and veterans, and make Oklahoma more affordable for every family,” Wilcox said.

Mazzei emerged from a brutal Republican primary runoff that he won by less than a point in August, giving him just more than two months until the general election. By comparison, Munson won the Democratic primary with over 74 percent of the vote in June.

“The president endorsed and picked the worst possible candidate out of the field of Republicans in Oklahoma,” the unnamed GOP strategist said.

“He’s going there to try to save his brand,” the strategist added. “It’s tighter than it should be.”

The Democratic Governors Association responded to the news of Trump’s visit in a statement, saying “Republicans are in full-on panic mode.”

The Republican National Committee announced on Tuesday that Trump will be visiting Grand Island, Neb. That state’s Senate race has received more attention as rising energy prices under the Trump administration threaten Republicans in agriculture-centric states.

In an interview with CNN’s Dana Bash on Tuesday, Nebraska’s incumbent Sen. Pete Ricketts (R) acknowledged the economic reality voters in his state are facing.

“There’s no doubt that high fuel prices put a strain on the budgets for every Nebraska family,” Ricketts told the network.

When asked about Trump’s campaign visit to Nebraska next week, Ricketts said, “We welcome him.”

articles.title: Election crime arrests keep piling up as Dems insist it 'just doesn't happen'
articles.summary: New federal cases charge noncitizens with voter fraud across multiple states, clashing with Democrats who oppose the SAVE Act and deny it happens.
articles.body: Federal authorities made arrests in a string of election-related indictments against noncitizens in recent weeks, colliding with Democratic claims ranging from such voting being "extremely rare" to assertions that it simply "doesn’t happen." The cases come amid a partisan fight over the SAVE Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. Democrats argue the measure would make voting harder for eligible Americans. "Let me be perfectly clear: This is a non-issue. Noncitizens do not vote in U.S. elections," Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon, D-Pa., declared in 2025 after voting 'no' on the bill at the time. Three noncitizens were arrested this month in Philadelphia County, which Scanlon partially represents, and charged with election-related offenses. BIDEN ADMINISTRATION GRANTED WOMAN GREEN CARD MONTHS BEFORE SHE ILLEGALLY VOTED IN 2024 ELECTION: DHS Trinidad and Tobago national Sade Guppy allegedly voted illegally in the 2022 midterms, while Haitian illegal immigrant Cliff Sanon was charged with submitting a fraudulent voter registration application prior to the 2026 Pennsylvania primary. DHS also pointed Fox News Digital to Mauritanian illegal immigrant Mahady Sacko, who is accused of voting in seven federal elections since 2008. Fox News Digital reached out to Scanlon for comment. On Wednesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced indictments of 10 foreign nationals accused of committing voter fraud in Minnesota alone, including during August's primary, saying the issue should not be a "partisan concept." The alleged illegal voters captured are from Brazil, Ghana, Germany, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Liberia and Canada. Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., has similarly called noncitizen voting "extremely rare" while denouncing the SAVE Act as "anti-voter" and claiming Trump is trying to "scapegoat immigrants." When asked Wednesday by Fox News Digital about the spate of arrests, Padilla reaffirmed the crime is "already illegal and every legitimate study shows it is extremely rare, despite Donald Trump’s claim to the contrary." "The Department of Justice’s arrest of a dozen people after investigating millions of the 174 million registered voters in America confirms that," he said, adding he wished the DOJ would instead focus on reported delays in voter-registration processing in states like Texas to ensure every eligible voter can vote. DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED Padilla called the recent announcement of 12 arrests a "desperate attempt by Republicans to distract from their record of rising costs, chaos, and corruption that are hurting the American people." Rep. Joe Morelle, D-N.Y., has called the SAVE Act "extremely dangerous" and "voter suppression." His office responded to Fox News Digital but did not offer comment before press time. Last month, Democratic Rep. James Walkinshaw of Fairfax County, Virginia, spoke out similarly on MS NOW. "It is so rare that it's almost impossible to measure. It just doesn’t happen," Walkinshaw said, surmising that Trump is trying to resurrect the "Big Lie" and "whining about the fact that he lost the 2020 election" by posturing to make similar claims after Republicans lose the midterms. Fox News Digital also sought comment from Walkinshaw and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., who said in March that "noncitizens do not vote in American elections." New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill also disclosed over the summer that roughly 400 noncitizens had voted in the state while resisting calls for additional federal scrutiny. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Three New Jersey residents were also charged this month with illegally voting and making false statements on citizenship applications. They hailed from Jamaica, Venezuela and Senegal. Asked about the dynamic, a DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital the agency could not comment on active investigations but remains committed to "rooting out and investigating election fraud wherever it can be found," demonstrating proof. "Despite the media and Democrats denying it for decades, noncitizens continue to register and vote in federal elections," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. Fox News' William Mears Jr. contributed to this report.

articles.title: How 16 undecided voters are weighing their 2026 election options
articles.summary: The voters, who participated in a recent NBC News poll and spoke to reporters afterward, are laser-focused on high prices and largely disappointed with both parties.
articles.body: James Morton isn’t sure which party he’s going to support in November’s elections, and he doesn’t like his options. Morton, a 67-year-old retired truck driver in Colorado, said Democrats have “gone too far to the left towards socialism,” while Republicans are “globalists” who “don’t care about the working-class people in this country.” Morton, an independent who voted for Donald Trump in 2024, is leaning toward backing third-party candidates in races for the House and the Senate this year. But he said his decision will come down to the high cost of living. “The No. 1 thing is getting the cost of things back down, inflation under control, and pretty much that’s it,” Morton said. He noted that he and his wife have been buying different groceries as they navigate high prices. Morton is among the 5% of voters surveyed last month in a national NBC News poll who said they weren’t sure which party they wanted to see controlling Congress after this year’s elections. NBC News spoke with 16 of those undecided voters as they weigh their votes this fall, some of whom declined to share their full names discussing politics. These voters feel little loyalty to either party — and many of them said that’s in part because they aren’t sure either party understands what’s important to them. Almost every one said high costs are top of mind. In the NBC News poll, 50% of voters said they wanted Democrats to win control of Congress in the midterms, while 45% said they wanted Republicans to have control. How the undecided voters in between resolve their strong, sometimes conflicting feelings could ultimately decide what Congress looks like in 2027, from who controls the majority to how many seats that party holds. Costs dominate Voters’ focus on making ends meet has been standing out in recent polling. In the latest NBC News survey, voters ranked cost of living and inflation as the most important issues facing the country, followed by government corruption and threats to democracy. “I don’t like how expensive things are, and I don’t think anyone does,” said Aidan Valenzuela, a 19-year-old security worker in Texas, who said he hasn’t decided whom to support in his state’s hotly contested races for governor and the Senate. Joanne, a 72-year-old Vermont independent who works for a heating company, said she plans to sit out her state’s governor’s race, and she hasn’t decided whom she’ll support farther down the ballot. “I just want somebody to bring some of these prices back down,” she said. Joanne said her husband relies on multiple medications, including insulin. “It’s pretty expensive and leaves nothing for anything else.” Luke Melanson, 49, of Louisiana, who is retired from construction work, said the rising cost of groceries has changed how he shops. “I’m not eating as much. I’m eating less food because I can only afford so much,” he said. Melanson doesn’t identify with either political party, instead considering himself a libertarian, and he declined to say where he was leaning in the midterm election. But he is frustrated with both parties and wants to see new candidates emerge who can personally relate to his financial position. “I want a plumber. I want someone that ran a smaller business, like a Kroger’s,” he said. “A teacher. I take anybody that isn’t a lawyer or someone so ultra-rich that the pay gap is so far they would never understand what I’m going through.” Meanwhile, South Carolinian Darien Thompson, a 25-year-old unarmed security guard at a mall, sees gas as the biggest financial woe of the moment. The cost of his commute is only going up. “It does take a mental load when it’s like, well, it’s going to cost this much to get to work and back, and I’m only making this much,” Thompson said. It doesn’t bode well for his long-term hopes of owning a home, and he doesn’t see any current politicians stepping up to tackle the issues in a way that has earned his support. “Politicians are getting into these petty squabbles,” he said. “But it’s, like, none of us can afford houses.” Thompson doesn’t see himself voting for a Republican in November, but he’s still undecided. He has leaned Democratic before, voting for then-Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024, but his vote this year will depend entirely on the specific candidate Democrats run in his area. Ibraham, a 42-year-old truck driver in Ohio who isn’t registered with either party, said he plans to back Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown in the Senate race in his state. Ibraham supported Harris in 2024 and said his vote this year is driven almost entirely by the surging price of diesel and a higher cost of living. “I’ve been driving for nine years. I’ve never seen anything like it. Never. Never, ever. Even during Covid, it didn’t get that high,” Ibraham said, noting that his weekly diesel costs have jumped from $2,000 to $3,500 or $3,700. “I’m spending an extra $1,500 on diesel every week. Just think about it — it’s a fortune,” he said. Down on both parties and Trump Ibraham described his support for Brown as more about opposing Republicans than endorsing Democrats, blaming the GOP-controlled White House and Congress for the current economic struggles. “It’s not about Brown,” Ibraham said of his Senate vote. “It’s just voting against the Republicans for what they’re doing. That’s it.” Other voters who were undecided but leaning toward Democrats expressed similar views, expressing caution and saying their potential support for Democrats was motivated more by reining in Trump and Republicans. Several voters — including those who backed Trump two years ago — specifically voiced concerns about Trump’s handling of the economy and the war in Iran. “I will probably support [a] Democrat this time around just so there’s some check and balances in place,” said Aaron L., a 30-year-old California independent who works in tech. He didn’t vote in 2024 while he was moving, but he said he most likely would have voted for Trump. But nearly two years into Trump’s second term, Aaron said, the economy is “a mess.” “It seems like the party, the Republican Party, just follow whatever Donald Trump says,” Aaron said. Like other undecided voters, Aaron said the economy and the war in Iran were among his top issues. Dissatisfaction with the war was high, including among Trump voters. “One of his platforms was no more useless wars, and here we are — we’re back,” said Kevin, a 35-year-old civil engineer in Massachusetts. Kevin, a Democrat, voted for Trump in 2024 hoping he would boost the economy. This year, he said, he is leaning toward supporting Republican Mike Minogue in the Massachusetts governor’s race, hoping he could shake up the state, and leaning toward backing Democratic Sen. Ed Markey for re-election. “It goes back to the checks and balances,” Kevin said of the possibility that he could split his ticket, saying he wants to see a Democratic-controlled Congress end the war in Iran. Kaleb Saracino, 21, of Nevada, doesn’t like how many resources are being poured into the Iran war or the idea that the U.S. is fighting there in behalf of Israel. He said he wants the government to cut off support for Israel, bring down costs and refocus on issues affecting everyday Americans. “The cost of groceries, the cost of gas, the cost of living have all gone up because of these endless wars,” Saracino said. Saracino knows he doesn’t want to support Trump, so he’s leaning toward the Democrats this year. But he doesn’t have warm feelings for either party. “They’re looking out for themselves, their careers, because they’re career politicians, not so much the betterment of the American people,” Saracino said about both Republicans and Democrats. Alexis, a 20-year-old college student in Florida, also expressed frustration with both parties in Washington. “They’ve made a bunch of promises that haven’t been fulfilled, and you know why? It’s because people cannot talk to each other these days. Congress is so divided,” she said. Alexis, an independent who voted for Harris in 2024, isn’t sure whom she’ll support in the Florida Senate race. She said more could get done “when we start allowing younger candidates who are more open-minded to vouching for the American people as a whole, rather than their own specific party.” Essen Zali, a 46-year-old IT consultant from Texas, voted for Joe Biden in 2020 but backed Trump in 2024 after he became frustrated with Biden during the conflict in Gaza. Now, the Iran war has again left him frustrated. “He went two steps forward with the whole war thing, and now we are all over the place,” he said. On top of that, Zali said, Trump seems focused on the wrong things. “All the construction work that was going on in Washington, that was not ever required. All the beautifications and everything, that’s secondary. The tariff war without a reason,” Zali said. “It seems like he is burning all the ships.” Connor Woodring, a 22-year-old independent from Colorado, also supported Trump in 2024. He was another voter who felt disdain for both parties. “They’re one on the same side of the same coin, basically. Republicans are the warmongering side of it. Democrats are the side that try to pull at your heartstrings,” he said. “Either way, they’re going to vote and do the same thing they’ve done for the last 50 years, so it doesn’t matter which side you vote in.” Woodring is a registered independent and doesn’t like any candidates in his area. His preference is to vote for someone not in either major party. But, he said, “there’s a lot that can happen between now and November.”

articles.title: Teen's tragic killing by illegal immigrant becomes flashpoint in battle for control of Congress
articles.summary: Sheridan Gorman's parents confronted Rep. Mike Lawler and Democrat Cait Conley over sanctuary city policies during a heated congressional debate.
articles.body: A teenage girl's tragic death, allegedly at the hands of an illegal immigrant who was previously deported from the U.S., has now become a political flashpoint in her hometown. Sheridan Gorman's grieving parents made their heartbreaking plea for change directly to the two candidates running to represent their district in suburban New York during an electoral debate earlier this week. They asked Democrat Cait Conley and incumbent Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., whether they supported ending New York State's law barring local law enforcement from cooperating with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The 18-year-old Loyola University student was shot and killed while walking with friends late at night near her Chicago college campus in March of this year. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has said the accused, Jose Medina, is a Venezuelan national who came to the U.S. illegally in May 2023 and was released by the prior administration. He was arrested for shoplifting in Chicago the next month but released again, DHS said. Both Chicago and Illinois are sanctuary jurisdictions, meaning law enforcement there are also barred from cooperating with ICE. GRIEVING PARENTS OF SLAIN STUDENT SHERIDAN GORMAN SPEAK OUT: 'WE CAN'T LET THIS HAPPEN TO ANOTHER FAMILY' Gorman's killing fast became a rallying cry for supporters of President Donald Trump's crackdown on illegal immigration. Lawler, who is fighting an uphill battle for a third term representing New York's 17th Congressional District, has also argued it is an example of what could happen more often if Democrats win control on Capitol Hill. "Look, I've been very clear there should be reforms of ICE. They should wear body cameras. They should not wear masks. They should wear uniforms. They shouldn't be going into places like the Home Depot parking lot. They should be very targeted in what they are doing. And states like New York should be cooperating with them to deport criminal illegal aliens," Lawler told Fox News Digital on Wednesday. "So look, I think the challenge here will be if Democrats win, they will do everything they can to return to the Biden-era of lax immigration policy, lax enforcement, and try to cut off the resources of ICE and [Border Patrol], and I, for one, just will not support that." DEM CANDIDATE CLEARS CROWDED FIELD TO FACE TRUMP-BACKED INCUMBENT IN NY His district could be one of the few that decides control of the House for the latter half of President Trump's final term. Gorman's parents tearfully said during his debate against Conley this week, "The man charged with her murder was here illegally and had previously been arrested for a crime and released under Chicago's sanctuary policies. A simple five-second phone call between local and federal law enforcement would have saved her life." Conley responded to them first, "My heart absolutely breaks, and what happened to Sheridan is inexcusable. Government failed her. And for that, we have to make sure that that doesn't happen again." WATCH: ANGEL MOM TURNS TABLES ON SANCTUARY POLITICIANS WITH BASIC QUESTION ABOUT THEIR PRIORITIES "Immigration enforcement is essential," she said, though added, "What is happening under this administration, unfortunately, is not a focus on violent criminals, but what we're seeing is them rolling up people like grandmas and nurses, people in our communities." Lawler then accused Conley of dodging the question, adding, "She does support Kathy Hochul's new law, and she would not support federal legislation to end sanctuary policies. Let me be very clear: I stand with you. I am against Kathy Hochul's disastrous new law, and I support any legislation that will end sanctuary jurisdictions in this country." DHS BOSS REVEALS OVAL OFFICE PLAN TO 'WITHHOLD FUNDING' FROM SANCTUARY CITIES AFTER AGGRESSIVE NEW YORK BUST It came weeks after the Gormans took the stage alongside Lawler at the GOP's 2026 midterm convention in Dallas, Texas. "The Gormans have more courage than any Democrat member of Congress who voted against protecting our citizens from criminal illegals," Lawler said in introducing them. "They are not running for office, but their story — Sheridan's story — is the direct result of bad policy. Policies we cannot afford to get back to every again." OUTGOING HOUSE DEMOCRAT BACKS INCUMBENT REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER FOR RE-ELECTION The teenager's story again popped up in new ads released by Lawler's campaign on Wednesday. In one of the spots, Gorman's mother tearfully tells the viewer, "He just shot her. Just shot her. Hunted her down. I thought I knew what sanctuary city policies are, I didn't." SHERIDAN GORMAN’S MOM SCORCHES DEM LAWMAKERS SHE SAYS REFUSED TO HEAR FAMILIES OF SLAIN AMERICANS "The sanctuary policies being pushed by Kathy Hochul and Democrats killed our daughter," her father said. "I couldn't protect her from these policies." Her mother added, "But Mike Lawler can." Illegal immigration was one of the top issues in 2024, and Republicans are trying to harness the same backlash from voters who opposed the Biden administration's more lax border policies.
